newsitem.title: USA: U.S. probes Iran deal that may provoke sanctions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. probes Iran deal that may provoke sanctions.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it was investigating whether sanctions should be imposed on a British-Canadian consortium under U.S. law for a deal with Iran to develop the Balal oil field.

"That's a very serious issue. And we're looking into it with great care right now, but we have not yet made a determination if this particular deal fits that category," spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
Under U.S. law, companies investing more than $40 million in oil or gas projects in Iran in any one year could be subject to sanctions.

"And our law is very clear. The Iran-Libya Sanctions Act sets a threshold for investment beyond which companies are technically in violation, and therefore can be subject to U.S. penalties," Burns said.
Iran's oil minister on Saturday said that Tehran had awarded a contract to British and Canadian firms to develop the offshore field. The project could cost $140 million or more.

The minister, Gholamreza Aghazadeh, refused to name the two firms, but sources at the National Iranian Oil Company identified them as Britain's Pell Frischmann and Canada's Bow Valley. U.S. officials said those were the firms referred to by Burns.
